findings.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 — A `t.Skip` for the postgres dbType is added in the same PR that changes resource-server init sequencing (Init now runs once at construction instead of per-RPC, and search-init/watcher-start order is swapped), so this skip likely masks a real regression from those changes rather than being a pre-existing unrelated flake, yet no investigation or linked issue is referenced.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:88 — BuildIndex`'s lock was narrowed from wrapping the whole build+cache-write to only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment, meaning two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key can now both build a full index in parallel (wasted work, and the last writer silently wins, discarding the other's index/resources); no concurrency or race-detector test exists in this repo to catch that behavior, and no bleve_test.go file is present at all.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Moving Init() to run exactly once inside NewResourceServer (and removing all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` guards) changes failure semantics from "lazily surfaced on first RPC, cached forever via sync.Once" to "construction hard-fails and returns nil server + error" — note the previous per-RPC calls never actually provided self-healing either, since sync.Once.Do never re-invokes its function after a failed first attempt, so no retry capability is actually lost. The real risk is that NewResourceServer's error is silently swallowed or ignored by some caller elsewhere in the (much larger) production codebase not present in this checkout (pkg/modules/, the DI wiring, are absent here), in which case a server value could be used with initErr permanently set and no per-call safety net remains; could not confirm or rule this out from the files available.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new postgres-specific `t.Skip` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO note (“test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.”) and no linked issue or explanation beyond that. In the same PR, substantial behavioral changes are made to resource-server initialization (calling `Init` once in `NewResourceServer`, removing per-RPC `Init` calls, and swapping search-init vs watcher start order). While the diff does not prove the postgres CI failure is caused by those changes, adding a skip here can indeed hide failures on postgres without documenting root cause or tracking it, which is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Moving Init() to run exactly once inside NewResourceServer (and removing all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` guards) changes failure semantics from "lazily surfaced on first RPC, cached forever via sync.Once" to "construction hard-fails and returns nil server + error" — note the previous per-RPC calls never actually provided self-healing either, since sync.Once.Do never re-invokes its function after a failed first attempt, so no retry capability is actually lost. The real risk is that NewResourceServer's error is silently swallowed or ignored by some caller elsewhere in the (much larger) production codebase not present in this checkout (pkg/modules/, the DI wiring, are absent here), in which case a server value could be used with initErr permanently set and no per-call safety net remains; could not confirm or rule this out from the files available.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes init timing/semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go ~255-263), and all per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards were removed across RPC handlers. That is a real behavior change from lazy, first-RPC initialization to eager, constructor-time failure. The finding’s stated *risk* (some external caller might ignore the returned error and still use the server, losing the per-call guard) is plausible in Go but cannot be verified from this diff because call sites aren’t shown.
